record._status: CLOSED — NO CHANGE MADE. Premise tested and rejected. The beige IS the product default; the library is right.
record._prompt: Build prompt asked to remove the beige default surface on the assumption it is used almost nowhere in production. Stop condition in the prompt: if code shows beige is the genuine default, report and stop. That condition was met.

whatTheBeigeIs.figmaVariable: color/background/default — VariableID:74:40, collection Tebra/Color, scopes [FRAME_FILL] only
whatTheBeigeIs.notToBeConfusedWith: action.selected #F0EEE8 (backbone 2, VariableID:74:42) and computed/alphaSelected12 (VariableID:196:3, same #F0EEE8). 25 nodes carry that colour across the library and every one is a selected state or a Chip default filled — a different token doing a different job. It was counted separately and is not part of this finding.

productionEvidence.verdict: Beige is the genuine default page canvas, established three independent ways.
productionEvidence.two_cssBaseline: packages/hooks/src/ThemeProvider/ThemeProvider.tsx renders <CssBaseline/>, which paints body with theme.palette.background.default. CssBaselineOverrides.ts overrides only *:focus-visible outlines and never touches background, so MUI stock behaviour stands. 35 packages reference a ThemeProvider.
productionEvidence.three_hardcodedPageShells: 20 of 38 root.component.css files set body (or the single-spa root div) to #E8E5DF. navigation-ui — the always-mounted shell — is one of them, so beige is the canvas under every screen regardless of which micro-frontend is active.
productionEvidence.consumers: 17 non-story files read background.default directly (bgcolor/backgroundColor). A further 9 design-system stories use it as the backdrop to demo components against.
productionEvidence.corroboration: TableOverrides.ts:14 sets MuiTableRow root to background.paper explicitly. A table only needs to declare itself white if the surface beneath it is not white. The theme assumes a non-paper canvas.

theRealInconsistency.finding: The drift is in the product, not the library, and it is an untokenised cool grey.
theRealInconsistency.tally: Of 38 root.component.css files: 20 use #E8E5DF (tokenised, backbone 3), 10 use #edeef1, 2 use #fbf9f8, 5 set no background rule, 1 uses var(--active-color) (composition-ui, a docs harness).
theRealInconsistency.edeef1: #edeef1 appears nowhere in the repo except those 10 root.component.css files. It is not in paletteValues.ts, has no Tebra name, and no theme entry. Packages: accounts-receivable, documents, facesheet, medications, mfa, not-found, patient-intake-admin, payments-onboarding, signin, worklist.
theRealInconsistency.consequence: Ten to twelve micro-frontends paint a page canvas that no token describes. Because navigation-ui sets beige on body and these set their own, which colour wins is a CSS load-order accident, not a decision.
theRealInconsistency.recommendedFix: NOT the fix this prompt proposed. The correct move is to converge the 12 untokenised shells onto background.default, or to decide #edeef1 is the real default and retoken it. Either way it is a product change, not a library change. Needs an intent decision before anyone acts.

figmaUsageAudit.method: Every one of the 11 pages walked node by node, fills and strokes, matching literal #E8E5DF/#F0EEE8 and bound variables 74:40, 74:42, 196:3.
figmaUsageAudit.pageCanvases: ALL 11 page canvases are #F5F5F5 — Figma default grey, untouched. The prompt premise that page canvases are beige is false.
